4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The sani buckets in the facility do not register on the inspector test strips at the beginning of the inspection. The PIC indicated that any time that they put the wiping cloths into the solution the concentration drops quickly. A bit of investigation was completed by the inspector using different buckets and cloths. It appear that the temperature of the initial solution is not allowing for an effective mixing of the chemicals. When both hot and cold water was turned on equally the solution produced regular concentrations of Quat in solution. These should be verified on an ongoing basis and the chemical company consulted to ensure longevity of the system, but this appears to have corrected the issue. The bubbles from the initial mixing also appear to be giving false readings when contacted by test strips. All of this has been discussed with the PIC and the buckets remade.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 3-403.11: (A) TCS FOOD cooked, cooled, and reheated shall be reheated to 165F for 15 seconds. (P) (B) If reheated with microwave, FOOD rotated, stirred, covered, and allowed to stand for 2 minutes covered. (P) (C) Commercially processed FOOD shall be reheated to 135F. (P) (D) Reheating may not exceed 2 hours.(P) (E) Unsliced portions of MEAT roasts may be reheated according to oven parameters and minimum TCS conditions. (C)  

On arrival chili and cheese packages are observed in the reheating hot water bath in the back of the facility. The bath is observed with water at 133F at that time. A discussion took place at this time. Per employees this is a “new” unit that was received from a different store. It was re-iterated by the inspector that the cheese must be brought from 41F-165F in a period no greater than 2 hours. Approximately 1.5 hours later the bath and cheese was checked again. The bath water had reached 159F and the surface of the cheese was at 154F. The cheese and chili were pulled and placed into the microwave to immediately be brought above 165F prior to the 2 hour time limit. The process at this time is still insufficient for reheating of TCS foods and needs adjusting or to be changed to comply with the 2017 FDA  Food Code. Per the PIC the machine will be turned up to ensure that reheating takes place in a safe time frame.

Cheese sauce is observed in the reheating bath at temperatures including 128F-153F. Water temperature is observed a approximately 162F. Discussion with the PIC indicated that they were not sure of how long the cheese sauce had been in the reheating process and that it was likely to be three hours. Inspector suggested a dry erase board or similar process for tracking the start of the reheating process as the bags are placed into the reheating bath as needed throughout the day, and not on a consistent schedule. Other items discussed included leaving the lid on the reheating bath to trap heat in the container as well as ensuring that the tub is not “floating” and maintains a seal around its edge to trap the steam/heat. The cheese sauce was discarded during the inspection to correct the violation for today. PIC is aware that TCS foods reheated in the facility need to be brought up to 165F within two hours for safety.

findings.comment:

findings.comment:

He was also instructed to prepare an ice bath to store the PHFs within this cooler until the cooler was down to temperature. 2) Observed Sara Lee White Sheet Cake that had been distributed into single service containers and sitting on the counter. The box for the cake stated that the item should be maintained in freezer or refridgerator. Manager researched the data sheet during inspection and the data sheet from Sara Lee specifically states the item should be held at 41F or below. The cake was discarded during the inspection. 
750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.
750-153(a) When using time as a control. Food shall be marked to indicate the time when  it was removed from a temperature controlled environment. Properly label food.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
Observed 3 containers filled with water and bags of vegetable soup that were made yesterday. The containers were drained and each bucket had a temperature taken between the bags since it would destroy product to open the bag. The temperatures between the thin, food grade plastic bags were 51F-55F. Employee stated that he had placed ice in them and put them in the cooler. There is no time/temperature monitoring for the cooling of this product. These products are distributed to Steak N' Shake's throughout the Springfield Area. A risk control plan should be implemented to ensure the proper cooling of these items. All items were taken to the dumpster for destruction. 48 gallons of vegetable soup was destroyed. 
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Gravy prepared this morning was cooling in the walkin cooler. Surface temperature was 74F; internal temperature was 108F. Time was not marked on the container. GM noted it was made around 6a. Two hour time frame to get below 70F was past. GM reheated the gravy to 165F and placed it on the front line for use. Leftover gravy was to be discarded at the end of breakfast. Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F/below w/in an additional 4 hrs. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs. 
The only way to know foods are properly cooling to benchmark temperatures in designated time frame is to monitor temperatures during cooling process with clean, calibrated stem thermometers. Separating foods into smaller batches, placing containers in ice baths, and stirring frequently will help speed up the cooling process. Cover containers loosely when foods are placed in the walkin to finish cooling, and continue stirring and checking temperatures. It is ok to leave containers of cooling food uncovered in coolers as long as the shelving above food is clean and no raw foods are stored above the cooked food.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.citation_text: 750.100 - Moldy tomatoes were observed in a plastic storage tub at back prep area. Tomatoes were discarded in the trash during the inspection. Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 (x4) - A) Pan of shredded cheese at prep cooler on cook line had an internal temperature of 55F. Cheese was double panned; pan holding cheese was not in contact with cold air in cooler. Cheese was discarded and replaced with fresh product. B) Top layers of individual half and halfs in the upper holding compartment of salad cooler had internal temperature 49F. Top layers were discarded by member of wait staff. Remaining packets (43F/below) were moved to top holding area, and packaged apple slices (not PHF) were placed in holding well below. **Do not over fill pans in upper holding compartment of salad cooler.** C) Container of blue cheese dressing sitting out by table mounted slicer by walkin cooler had internal temperature of 47F-48F. No staff took ownership for removing container from walkin cooler. Label on package stated "must be refrigerated at all times." Dressing was placed back in the walkin cooler by inspector. D) Three pans of steak burgers in the Blodgett brand oven at back prep had internal temperatures of 53F-60F. It appeared the oven was set to blow cooler air around the pans (possibly for thawing purposes). Manager discarded all burgers in the trash. Cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) must be maintained at 41F/bwlow at all times. Maintain PHF at proper holding temperatures.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.citation_text:
750.240 - A) Pans of raw steak burgers were thawing at room temperature on top of soda syrup boxes in storage area by walkin cooler. Three pans were also observed inside the Blodgett brand oven with cold air circulating around them. Steak burgers in the oven were discarded (see #3a Part D). Pans with other steak burgers (internal temperatures 35F-44F) were either moved to front line for use or placed in walkin cooler to finish properly thawing. PHF shall be properly thawed by one of the following: 1. Under refrigeration 41F/below, 2. Under  potable running water 70F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, or 4. As part of the cooking process.
B) Employee placed two large containers of vanilla ice cream in a bus tub on the floor in front of the sundae freezers. Employee noted she did so in order to soften the product. Employee and manager were advised ice cream must be placed in walkin cooler or another refrigeration unit to soften product before use. PHF must not be left out at room temperature to thaw for any reason and should never be stored in bus tubs on the floor.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text: 750.130 - (x2) A) Pans of raw steak burgers were thawing at room temperature sitting on top of soda syrup boxes in storage area by walkin cooler. Pans of burgers were moved to walkin cooler (see #6). B) Flat of raw eggs in walkin cooler was on a shelf above what appeared to be bags of commercially processed sauces. Eggs were moved to proper storage area. All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination. Do not store raw eggs and meats next to, above, or on top of ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - A) Foods were uncovered in multiple coolers and freezers. Cover foods between uses, during slow periods, and during extended storage (walkin cooler, walkin freezer, etc.) to protect products from potential contamination. B) Bus tub with 2 large containers of vanilla ice cream was observed on the floor in front of sundae station freezers. Tub was moved to a proper cold holding unit. C) Cases of chili beans were observed on the floor at back prep area. Cases were placed in proper storage area. Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the ground, in a clean covered container, and protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750.160b & 530a - A) HANDWASHING & GLOVE USE (x2) 1. Cook at grill was observed going between multiple orders and touching various foods and general surfaces with the same pair of gloves. When advised on proper glove use, cook changed gloves but did not wash hands. 2. Employee on food assembly line (at far end by drive thru) did not change gloves between handling a wet wiping cloth and returning to food prep/handling. Hands were being used for contact with multiple products. Employee was advised on proper use of gloves and changed gloves at request of inspector. Gloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations. Employees shall properly wash their hands before putting on gloves, between glove changes, prior to handling food or clean equipment, and any time hands may have been contaminated.
B) Employee working in dish area was observed eating. Employee moved plate of food to break area and stopped eating in the dish area. Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: 750.530b - Personal drink without a lid or straw was observed on the bread storage shelf in the back prep area. Cup was discarded in the trash by inspector. Employees may drink from closed beverage containers with a lid and straw as long as the containers are handled to prevent contamination of hands, containers, and exposed food.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - Wet wiping cloths were observed sitting out on counters and at prep sinks throughout the facility. Store wiping cloths in sanitizer solution between uses to inhibit the growth of microorganisms between uses. If spray bottles of sanitizer are used for wiping surfaces, then disposable paper towels must be used and discarded after each use.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris. **In-use equipment and utensils (i.e. cutting boards, knives, can opener, etc.) must go through ware washing process up to every 4hrs.**

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

Clean all non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.citation_text: 750.1120 - A) Evidence of handsinks being used to rinse food utensils was observed. Upon arrival of inspector a spatula with food debris on it was noted in the back handsink. A whisk was observed in the handsink at the front counter. Food utensils were removed from sinks and placed in dish area to go through proper ware washing. B) Employee was observed emptying a chemical bottle in the back handsink. Employee took bottle to dish area to finish emptying bottle per request of inspector. Management and staff were once again advised on proper use of handsinks. Handsinks are to be used for handwashing only and must always be accessible. Handsinks are not to be used for rinsing utensils, emptying chemical bottles, filling pitchers with water, or any other tasks. The only time a handsink should ever be unaccessible is when someone is waiting to wash his/her hands because another person is already in the process of properly washing their hands.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly

findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Three plastic 5 gallon buckets of cooked noodles in walkin cooler had internal temperatures at 102F, 106F, & 126F. findings.citation_text: 750.130 - Unlabeled container of white granular substance was observed on the bottom shelf of a prep table (same area where chemical bottles were noted to be stored in #41a). Manager thought it might be salt.  Unless the identity of a food is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the original packaging, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name. Maintain proper labels on all bulk foods, especially clear and white liquids and powders.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Shell eggs in cold holding well between grill & steam table had surface temperatures of 56F to 61F. Internal temperature for a cracked egg was 56F. Eggs had been in the holding well for approximately 1.5hrs when checked at 10:45am. Eggs were discarded at 11am (end of breakfast). Egg substitute also had an internal temperature of 56F and was discarded. Cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) must be maintained at 41F/below unless time is being used as a control. Maintain cold PHF at proper temperature.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Cold holding well between grill and steam table was holding at 50F in the bottom according to inspector's stem thermometer. Unit did not have a hanging thermometer in the bottom for comparison, but PHF was not holding at proper temperature (see #3a). Manager noted a call for service would be made for the cold holding well. All refrigeration units used to store PHF shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41F/below. Use time control and use/discard PHF within 4 hours when placed in the well until it is able to maintain 41F/below. Due to location of the well it would be helpful to not only maintain lids on products between uses but also add ice in the bottom of the well to help maintain colder temperatures.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Facility did not have a thermometer down inside cold holding well between steam table and grill. findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text: 750.1160 - Fruit flies were observed at various locations - 1 in dish area, 1 at clean pan/utensil storage across from ice machine, 2 handsink & table across from sundae prep, and 5-6 around steam table/steam kettle area. Manager noted container with soiled wiping cloths had been an issue and was to be removed from the facility by Friday. Clean all floor drains throughout, and properly store wet mops and wiping cloths between uses. If thorough cleaning alone does not alleviate the issue then contact PCO for service.
